title: Ellington sessions of January to March 1928
summary: Willard reads the discography for 'Bugle Call Rag', 'Take It Easy' and 'Jubilee Stomp'; Bigard says the process allowed only a snare drum, not a bass drum, and recalls the band's personnel.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: "Bugle Call Rag" was, of course, January 9, 1928, --
-- at the same time as "Sweet Mama" and "Stack-n-lee Blues"
Is that the way you remember three numbers on that date?
No? Because you're listed on all of them. Are they right or not?
Uh-huh. "Bugle Call Rag," "Stack-o-Lee Blues," and "Sweet Mama".
I know Freddie Guy was on that date, Bubber Miley.
Yeah. Otto Hardwick, Harry Carney, Barney Bigard, L. M. -- who's L. M., this is all initials. -- Bubber Miley, Joe Nanton, Duke Ellington (inaudible), Freddie Guy, Wellman Braud, and Sonny Greer.
So, but this says -- on all of them it says Wellman
But you said that the recording process couldn't handle the bass and drums. How that work out?
They've got the names listed as personnel on the record.
Well, they could use only the snare drum. They couldn't use the bass drum.
And then the next session after that was 10 days later, January 19. 'Take It Easy', 'Jubilee Stomp', 'Harlem Twist'.

And then in February -- they don't have a date in February -- 'East St. Louis Toodle-Oo', 'Jubilee Stomp', 'Take It Easy'. And then in March Take It Easy again. And these were all -- and 'Jubilee Stomp' again.
No, we only recorded that once unless they re-recorded or something.
